# Code Review Report

## Review Summary

This branch is well-scoped and the extraction of Phase 7f into a dedicated subagent is directionally correct, but the new agent contract is not yet executable as written. Two runtime-blocking instruction defects remain in the `quality-reviewer` workflow, and the acceptance semantics still do not match the documented "best-scoring version" behaviour.

**Files Reviewed:** 4
**Findings:** 2 Critical, 1 Warning, 0 Suggestion

## Findings

### Critical Findings

[C-01] `quality-reviewer` Calls `parse-scores` With an Unsupported Contract
Category: Correctness
Severity: Critical
File: .opencode/agents/quality-reviewer.md
Lines: 63-68
Description: Step 2b tells the subagent to call `critique-runner` with `operation: "parse-scores"`, `name`, and `iteration`, then record the returned score. That is not the actual tool contract. The Python CLI and TypeScript wrapper require `criticType` and `responseText` for `parse-scores`; they do not support loading aggregate results from a savepoint. As written, the first review iteration will fail at this step with `--critic-type required for parse-scores` / `--response-text required for parse-scores`, so the new Phase 7f loop cannot complete.
Suggestion: Remove the `parse-scores` step and read the aggregate score from the `run-critics` result or saved critique payload, or extend `critique-runner` with a real aggregate score-reading operation and update both the tool contract and agent instructions together.

[C-02] Chapter Quality Loop Never Switches `critique-runner` Into Chapter Mode
Category: Correctness
Severity: Critical
File: .opencode/agents/quality-reviewer.md
Lines: 56-75, 87-90
Description: Every `critique-runner` call in the new subagent omits `mode: "chapter"`. The tool defaults to `outline`, so the Phase 7f flow will run the outline critic set, use the outline savepoint namespace, and evaluate the wrong artifact type even though the agent is supposed to review an assembled chapter. This breaks the core purpose of the extracted subagent.
Suggestion: Pass `mode: "chapter"` on every `critique-runner` invocation in this workflow (`run-critics`, `should-refine`, `generate-feedback`, and any replacement for the current parse/read step).

### Warning Findings

[W-01] Best Score Is Tracked, But the Best-Scoring Chapter Text Is Never Preserved
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/agents/quality-reviewer.md
Lines: general
Description: The workflow initialises `best_score`, updates it when a higher score appears, and returns `accepted_chapter_text` plus `best_score`. However, it never stores the chapter text associated with that best score; it only keeps `current_chapter_text`, which is the latest revision. If the final revision scores worse than an earlier draft and the loop exits because `chapter_max_revisions` is exhausted, the agent will return the last draft rather than the best-scoring one. That also contradicts the feature documentation in `docs/features/story-orchestrator.md`, which promises that the best-scoring version is accepted when the cap is reached.
Suggestion: Track `best_chapter_text` alongside `best_score` and return that text when the loop exits on revision-cap exhaustion, or remove the "best-scoring version" claim from the documentation if last-draft acceptance is the intended behaviour.

## Overall Assessment

Not ready for merge. The new Phase 7f extraction is conceptually sound, but the subagent currently instructs an impossible `critique-runner parse-scores` call and never opts into chapter mode, so the runtime path it introduces is broken before the first full iteration completes. After those contract defects are fixed, the branch still needs one more pass on acceptance semantics so the returned chapter text matches the documented "best version wins" behaviour.
